propositions: Handing a resumption the prior attempt's search frontier as a data-shaped exclusion list inside an untrusted fence does not reduce re-search overlap rate or attempts-to-clean-close compared to cache-seeded control across test corpus tickets.
The frontier block acts as a signpost, causing the model to immediately re-read and re-search files and patterns listed as already-examined, raising measured overlap rather than reducing it.

The cache-seeding mechanism (locust behavior) already removes the dominant redundancy by skipping re-verification of credited criteria; remaining re-grounding of unproven criteria cannot be suppressed by an inert data-shaped evidence block.
Measured overlap rate worsens or shows no improvement for both corpus tickets (45c1: +78% relative increase, 8d74: +60% relative increase) when treatment arm receives frontier block versus control.
